# Independent audit: same-parity section contacts below the OC budget

Audited `candidate f32902d5e2b99bcc`
in full, including its all-cap argument and T>=1 extension. Result: PASS.
The exact verifier `supporting computation verify_multidimensional_section_barycenter_parity.py`
was also rerun successfully. This is an auxiliary counterexample, not
an OC counterexample or a counterexample involving global deepest points.

## Independent all-cap check

The actual polytope

    C_T={|z_i|<=2, ||z||_infinity-2<=x<=T}

is convex, bounded and full dimensional. Its integer fibers and three
product layers are exactly as stated. All 625 fibers are positive;
the mixed mass is 82+625T, and the cap x<=0 has mass 82. The points
(+-e_1,0) and their integer midpoint lie in proper fibers.

For T=1 and downward caps through (e_1,0), the gain/loss identity

    F(a)=82+G(a)-L(a)-phi(a_1-1)

is exact, including the otherwise easily omitted bottom unit interval
at z=0. The gain estimate G>=125 phi(A), A=||a||_infinity, follows
from two faces in a largest-coefficient direction and reflection of
the remaining three coordinates. The scalar inequality
phi(A+t)+phi(-t)>=phi(A) has the correct sign for all real t.

Independently, convex maximization over the coefficient cube gives
sum_(z in {-1,0,1}^4)(a_1-a.z)_+<=102A. The exact coefficient counts
1,4,10,16,19,16,10,4,1 give 102 when a_1=1 and 21 when a_1=-1.
Combining this with L<=81 and the bottom loss yields the stated
F(a)>=82+22 min(A,1). In particular this is a GLOBAL minimizing-cap
proof, not an inference from a Clarke stationary point.

Upward caps retain at least 125T from the two paired positive-layer
faces: their paired thresholds sum to -|a_1|, so the clipped excluded
lengths sum to at most T. The vertical limit correctly gives only a
lower bound on a closed vertical cap, because whole boundary fibers
must be retained. That lower bound still exceeds 82. Translating any
containing halfspace through the candidate completes the all-cap proof.

Increasing T only adds source mass outside the fixed cap x<=0. For
every cap through either candidate its unnormalized mass therefore
cannot decrease, while the chosen cap remains exactly 82. This proves
the minimizing-cap assertion for every T>=1 without extrapolating a
local section argument. Reflection gives the second candidate.

## Section weights and scope

The 81 proper sections have weight one. The remaining 544 supporting
sections split into slice counts 125,98,98,98,125. The displayed
traces have total effective weight and first-coordinate moment both
105547/397. All other moments vanish by reflection.

The trace array is a convex combination of FOUR actual limiting
differentiability gradients, using the stated base-ten perturbations.
Its two averaged first gradients are 44 and -750, and weights
375/397 and 22/397 cancel them exactly. No independent, incompatible
choice of boundary signs is used. The positive trace margins give the
strict local minimum as well. The higher-continuous-dimensional product
extension makes only a local full-normal assertion; that assertion
follows by integrating the absolute-value lower bound over the full
cube, and does not import the d=1 global calculation.

At T=5,

    depth(+-e_1,0)=depth(0,0)=82/3207<1/32,

with the strict integer check 2624<3207. Thus small cap budget alone
does not exclude same-parity proper section barycenters or repair
strict intermediate-integer interpolation at arbitrary points.

The global-maximizer qualification is essential and is explicitly
unresolved by this example. The centrally symmetric positive-layer
submeasure gives

    depth(0,T/2)=625T/[2(82+625T)]>82/(82+625T).

Its lower bound holds for every closed ambient halfspace, including
boundary mass, and the cap x>=T/2 supplies equality. Hence the two
same-parity candidates are definitely NOT global mixed-depth maximizers.
